rulings.rationale: Keep the formal heading distinct from the first oracle, while requiring the full chapter-one judgment complex whenever the notice is interpreted.
rulings.counterevidence: The superscription governs the whole book and therefore still requires book-level context.

rulings.rationale: Surface the sweeping creature register together because its repeated verb and closing formula complete before the oracle narrows to Judah and Jerusalem.
rulings.counterevidence: Cutting-off language continues into 1:4, but the geographic and object narrowing is the stronger surface seam.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Zeph.1.1-Zeph.1.3; Zeph.1.2-Zeph.1.6; Separate chunks for members of the creature register

rulings.rationale: Retain the cultic and non-seeking accusations as one localized indictment; splitting the coordinated catalogue would conceal its single geographic and rhetorical scope.
rulings.counterevidence: The catalogue moves from named practices to the broader failure to seek, creating internal variation but not a stronger surface boundary.

rulings.rationale: The hush command belongs with its prepared-sacrifice and punishment tableau, not as a detached silence maxim or an undifferentiated part of the entire day sequence.
rulings.counterevidence: Day language continues throughout 1:10-18, requiring the larger day-complex parent.

rulings.rationale: City cries, commercial collapse, interior lamp search, quoted complacency, and property reversal jointly carry the Jerusalem movement to the great-day restart.
rulings.counterevidence: The move from public soundscape to private lamp search at 1:12 is a recoverable internal turn.

rulings.rationale: The repeated day descriptions accumulate into one battle-and-darkness poem; the consequence stanza supplies its ending rather than a new standalone oracle.
rulings.counterevidence: The consequences in 1:17-18 could be treated as a dependent concluding stanza.

rulings.rationale: Gathering urgency and the threefold seek response answer one another, so the appeal closes at possible concealment before the nations rationale begins.
rulings.counterevidence: The terse wording and addressee scope of 2:1 remain translation-sensitive without changing the surface boundary.

rulings.rationale: The named Philistine cities initiate the coastland judgment that resolves in Judah-remnant reversal; the 2:4 paragraph seam remains a child, not the surfaced boundary.
rulings.counterevidence: The WLC-family samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 support a real dependent child seam; that seam is preserved as dissent rather than erased.

rulings.rationale: The widened worship horizon completes the Moab-Ammon reproach and reversal, whereas separating 2:11 would strip the oracle of its rhetorical outcome.
rulings.counterevidence: Zeph.2.11 broadens beyond Moab and Ammon and could be retained as a dependent concluding horizon child.

rulings.rationale: Direct second-person address and the northward change make the terse Cush saying retrievable, but its nations-cycle parent remains mandatory because the unit is so compact.
rulings.counterevidence: Its brevity makes isolated retrieval risky; it must retain nations-cycle hydration and cannot authorize historical or ethnic conclusions.

rulings.rationale: Nineveh desolation, animal habitation, exposed architecture, proud self-speech, and passerby taunt work as one northern-city oracle rather than separate image fragments.
rulings.counterevidence: The city self-speech at 2:15 is a strong internal rhetorical turn.

rulings.rationale: The righteous-Yahweh contrast answers the rebellious-city and leadership accusations, so 3:5 closes the woe rather than forming an independent characterization.
rulings.counterevidence: Zeph.3.5 changes from accusation to divine contrast and remains a recoverable dependent turn.

rulings.rationale: Destroyed-nations example, intended correction, and corrupt response form a complete warning movement before the inferential wait summons changes function.
rulings.counterevidence: Pronoun and causal scope link the movement backward to the city woe and forward to the therefore clause.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Attach Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.7 wholly to Zeph.3.1-Zeph.3.5; Attach Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.7 wholly to Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13; Separate the correction quotation from its failed response

rulings.rationale: Zephaniah 3:8 is exposed as a judicial hinge because it gathers failed correction into assembly and fire before 3:9 turns to purification; parent hydration protects both dependencies.
rulings.counterevidence: The verse depends strongly on both neighboring movements and must never surface without the Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 parent.

rulings.rationale: Purified speech, shared service, and dispersed worshipers form the first promise child, ending where the in-that-day formula and city address reset the discourse.
rulings.counterevidence: Purification, pride removal, and remnant formation remain one larger restoration sequence, so the canonical lane's whole Zeph.3.9-Zeph.3.13 surface remains a defensible dissent.

rulings.rationale: Proud removal and the humble remnant belong together through truthful speech, rest, safety, and marked closure; merging backward would erase the 3:11 address turn.
rulings.counterevidence: The unit is causally continuous with purification in 3:9-10 and cannot be treated as an independent identity proposition.

rulings.rationale: The reported reassurance at 3:16 supplies the Zion song with its saving-presence ground, so it remains an internal speech seam within the complete rejoicing movement.
rulings.counterevidence: The in-that-day report at 3:16 is a genuine internal speech seam and supports the canonical lane's proposed child division.

rulings.rationale: Difficult 3:18 wording is kept with rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the final speech formula, preserving a closing restoration unit without settling its translation.
rulings.counterevidence: The syntax and subject scope of Zeph.3.18 are difficult and may connect backward to the song or its festal setting; this lowers confidence but does not presently require a boundary hold.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Attach Zeph.3.18 to Zeph.3.14-Zeph.3.17; Zeph.3.19-Zeph.3.20; Detach Zeph.3.20 as an isolated promise
